scope: Catalog actions from a cross-family blind discovery of local-model workloads beyond memory and RAG on the 64 GB M5 Pro, for the US-equities north star and native agent engineering. One frozen packet went to a Claude Opus 5.5 lane and a Codex GPT-6 Astra lane; one disagreement was adjudicated blind by GPT-6 Sol in three presentation orders, including a reversed listing; the coordinator's convergence table sets each record's decision. Discovery evidence only: nothing was installed, downloaded or executed for these items, inclusion selects nothing, and no record changes a default, the installed stack or the runtime target.

decision_values.converged_trial: Both lanes independently proposed the workload as a local trial; the record is a default, challenger or runtime the convergence table names. A measured trial against the acceptance gate precedes any adoption.
decision_values.adjudicated_skip: The lanes disagreed; a blind judge preferred the skip return in all three presentation orders (original, label-swapped and reversed listing).
decision_values.single_lane_lead: Proposed by one lane only; not converged; discovery only.
decision_values.skip_not_local: A lane named the workload as not worth running locally given the cloud frontier models.

evidence_levels.discovery_web_research: Named by a blind lane's web research on 2026-09-24 and checked only against the lane returns; no pinned source was read. Pins are live GitHub and Hugging Face API metadata (existence, head or revision, reported license), not a source review.

pin_method.github: gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/commits/HEAD --jq .sha for the default-branch head, and repos/OWNER/REPO for the default branch, archive state and reported license
pin_method.huggingface: https://huggingface.co/api/models/ORG/NAME .sha for the main revision; the author listings (api/models?author=...) for the dated checkpoint series and api/models/.../refs for branches

registration: Only /repository_decisions is registered with the decision index (python3 scripts/catalog_decisions.py --write --supplement catalogs/us-equities/local-model-workloads-20260924.json#/repository_decisions), because the union accepts only records that name a GitHub repository. PaddlePaddle/PaddleOCR and amazon-science/chronos-forecasting were already in the union; the other seven enter as research-supplement identities (850 to 857). /non_repository_decisions holds Hugging Face models pinned by revision and the workloads the lanes keep off the Mac, as data. /lane_mentions_not_recorded lists what the lanes named but the convergence table did not carry; it is not registered.

repository_decisions.workload: Catalyst tagging and extraction from 8-Ks and releases (ex-post labels, never live signals)
repository_decisions.role: Challenger: CPU span-extraction model (checkpoint gliner2.5-base-v1) as a distilled student for the backfill
repository_decisions.claude_disposition: trial; runner-up as a CPU encoder distilled student
repository_decisions.acceptance_gate: Convergence table: 1,000 stratified 8-Ks plus 300 hand-checked, macro-F1 against frontier labels. Claude lane: 1,000 stratified 2025–26 8-Ks from Massive plus 300 hand-checked; baselines Opus 5.5 labels and Massive tags; macro-F1, field exact match and filings/hour; adopt for backfill if F1 ≥0.9× Opus. Codex lane: 1,000 manually adjudicated 2024–2025 SEC/news passages including negatives, compared with keyword rules and frontier extraction; ≥95% catalyst recall, ≥90% precision, source-span accuracy and lower cost per document.
repository_decisions.reason: Both lanes rank catalyst extraction among the directly measurable local workloads. The Codex lane picks GLiNER2 first; the Claude lane uses it as the CPU student behind Qwen3.8-27B, which the convergence table keeps as the default.
limitations: Financial catalyst accuracy is unknown; the only scores are maker-reported general benchmarks (GLiNER2.5: Few-NERD F1 55.14, 16-task average 54.87) and the EMNLP 2025 demo paper.
M5 Pro throughput is unknown; the Codex lane warns against transferring older GLiNER speed claims.
The checkpoint's main revision was modified on 2026-09-24, the day of the lanes; the pin is that revision, not a tagged release.
Labels are ex-post research annotations for +200% movers, never live or backtest signals.

repository_decisions.workload: Tabular foundation models for +200% mover prediction
repository_decisions.role: The Codex lane's first choice, TabICLv2 (checkpoint 20260212)
repository_decisions.claude_disposition: skip: trees and deep nets still win on temporal, non-IID, large data (BeyondArena)
repository_decisions.codex_disposition: trial; best candidate (research challenger, permissive license)
repository_decisions.adjudicated_disposition: skip in all three presentation orders, including a reversed listing (gpt-6-sol, high effort)
repository_decisions.acceptance_gate: Skipped until a walk-forward comparison beats CatBoost (convergence table). If reopened, the Codex lane's test: point-in-time 2015–2025 equities features predicting +200% within 20 sessions, with delistings, temporal splits and a 20-session embargo; beat logistic regression and CatBoost on PR-AUC and Brier score.
repository_decisions.reason: The judge found BeyondArena's temporal, non-IID and large-data results closest to this task, and TabPFN-3.5's own report says tuned MLPs still lead its temporal and large subsets; TabICLv2's TabArena and TALENT wins do not establish an equities advantage.
limitations: One judge model from the Codex lane's family; listing position and letter labels were counterbalanced across three judgments for this question.
No cited paper tests rare +200% equity events with PR-AUC and Brier score; the skip rests on the closest evidence (reversed-listing judgment).
GitHub reports the license as NOASSERTION; the Codex lane calls it permissive.
TabICL's speed claim (under 10 s for 50K×100) is on an H100, not this Mac.
